subject: maths
title: Basic Probability
welcome_lead: How likely is something to happen? Probability turns chance into a number between 0 and 1.
meta_desc: Learn basic probability and sample space in this KS3 maths adventure.
final_note: Excellent! You can now measure chance with confidence.

concepts.def: A number from 0 to 1 showing how likely an event is.
A possible result of an experiment.
A set of outcomes we are interested.
The full list of all possible outcomes.
Outcomes that match the event we want.
All outcomes have equal chance of happening.

walkthroughs.body_html:
P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

Example: P(rolling a 6 on a fair die) = 1 ÷ 6 = 1/6.

For a coin flip, the sample space is {Heads, Tails}.

For a die roll, it is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

P(even on die) = 3/6 = 1/2.

Probability runs from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

0.5 means equally likely, like flipping heads on a fair coin.
